samples.question: The picture shows a board with seven columns, marked by seven faint vertical guide lines and by the seven grey chutes drawn in a row along the bottom. Number the columns and their chutes 1 to 7 from left to right. A blue ball is drawn above the board: the ball starts in the column whose guide line is nearest to the centre of the blue ball. On the board there are five levels of arrows, and the ball falls through the levels from top to bottom, as the grey arrow in the left margin shows. Each arrow is drawn in one column of one level; an orange arrow points right and a purple arrow points left. On each level, only the arrow standing in the ball's own column has any effect: that arrow pushes the ball one column in the direction it points, and the ball then falls on to the next level from its new column. Every other arrow on that level does nothing to this ball. If there is no arrow in the ball's column on a level, the ball falls straight down to the next level. No arrow in the picture would push the ball off the side of the board, and no arrow on a level can push the ball into another arrow of that same level, so at most one arrow acts per level. The arrows never move, and the ball is drawn only once, in its starting column; no later position of the ball is drawn anywhere. After the ball has fallen through all five levels, which numbered chute does it land in? Answer with a single number from 1 to 7, counting chutes from the left.
